verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם אֶבְחֲרָ֣ה נָּ֗א שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֙לֶף֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְאָק֛וּמָה וְאֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אַחֲרֵי־ דָוִ֖ד הַלָּֽיְלָה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lōm ’eḇ·ḥă·rāh nā šə·nêm- ‘ā·śār ’e·lep̄ ’îš wə·’ā·qū·māh wə·’er·də·p̄āh ’a·ḥă·rê- ḏā·wiḏ hal·lā·yə·lāh
verses.literal: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom Let me choose . . . twelve . . . thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of . . . David
verses.literalPt: Disse também Aitofel a Absalão: Deixa-me escolher doze mil homens, e me levantarei e perseguirei a Davi esta noite.

verses.original: וְאָב֣וֹא עָלָ֗יו וְה֤וּא יָגֵ֙עַ֙ וּרְפֵ֣ה יָדַ֔יִם וְהַֽחֲרַדְתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ וְנָ֖ס כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֑וֹ וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’ā·ḇō·w ‘ā·lāw wə·hū yā·ḡê·a‘ ū·rə·p̄êh yā·ḏa·yim wə·ha·ḥă·raḏ·tî ’ō·ṯōw wə·nās kāl- hā·‘ām ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw wə·hik·kê·ṯî ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ lə·ḇad·dōw
verses.literal: I will attack him . . . while he is weak . . . and weary I will throw him into a panic and all the people with him will flee I will strike down only the king
verses.literalPt: Virei sobre ele, enquanto está cansado e frouxo de mãos, e o espantarei. Fugirá todo o povo que está com ele; e ferirei tão somente ao rei.

verses.original: וְאָשִׁ֥יבָה כָל־ הָעָ֖ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ כְּשׁ֣וּב הַכֹּ֔ל הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’ā·šî·ḇāh ḵāl hā·‘ām ’ê·le·ḵā kə·šūḇ hak·kōl hā·’îš ’ă·šer ’at·tāh mə·ḇaq·qêš kāl- hā·‘ām yih·yeh šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband You seek the life of only one man . . . then all the people will be at peace
verses.literalPt: Farei tornar a ti todo o povo como todo o povo costuma voltar (é o que tu buscas), e todo o povo ficará em paz.

verses.original: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yî·šar had·dā·ḇār bə·‘ê·nê ’aḇ·šā·lōm ū·ḇə·‘ê·nê kāl- ziq·nê yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: This proposal seemed good to Absalom . . . and all the elders of Israel
verses.literalPt: O parecer agradou a Absalão e a todos os anciãos de Israel.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם קְרָ֣א נָ֔א גַּ֖ם לְחוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֑י וְנִשְׁמְעָ֥ה מַה־ בְּפִ֖יו גַּם־ הֽוּא׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm qə·rā nā gam lə·ḥū·šay hā·’ar·kî wə·niš·mə·‘āh mah- bə·p̄îw gam- hū
verses.literal: Then Absalom said Summon . . . Hushai the Archite as well and let us hear what he too has to say
verses.literalPt: Disse Absalão: Chamai, agora, a Husai, arquita, e ouçamos também o que ele diz.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלוֹם֒ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל הֲנַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־ דְּבָר֑וֹ אִם־ אַ֖יִן אַתָּ֥ה דַבֵּֽר׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ḥū·šay ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’ê·lāw lê·mōr kad·dā·ḇār haz·zeh dib·ber ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el hă·na·‘ă·śeh ’eṯ- də·ḇā·rōw ’im- ’a·yin ’at·tāh ḏab·bêr
verses.literal: So Hushai came to Absalom who . . . . . . told him Ahithophel has spoken this proposal Should we carry it out - If not what do you say
verses.literalPt: Tendo Husai chegado à presença de Absalão, disse-lhe Absalão: Desta maneira falou Aitofel: Seguiremos o seu conselho? Se não, fala tu.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חוּשַׁ֖י אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא־ טוֹבָ֧ה הָעֵצָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ יָעַ֥ץ אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל בַּפַּ֥עַם הַזֹּֽאת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥū·šay ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm lō- ṭō·w·ḇāh hā·‘ê·ṣāh ’ă·šer- yā·‘aṣ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el bap·pa·‘am haz·zōṯ
verses.literal: Hushai replied - This time the advice of Ahithophel . . . is not sound
verses.literalPt: Husai respondeu a Absalão: Não é bom o conselho que Aitofel deu esta vez.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אַתָּ֣ה יָ֠דַעְתָּ אֶת־ אָבִ֨יךָ וְאֶת־ אֲנָשָׁ֜יו כִּ֧י גִבֹּרִ֣ים הֵ֗מָּה וּמָרֵ֥י נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ הֵ֔מָּה כְּדֹ֥ב שַׁכּ֖וּל בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְאָבִ֙יךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יָלִ֖ין אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥū·šay ’at·tāh yā·ḏa‘·tā ’eṯ- ’ā·ḇî·ḵā wə·’eṯ- ’ă·nā·šāw kî ḡib·bō·rîm hêm·māh ū·mā·rê ne·p̄eš hêm·māh kə·ḏōḇ šak·kūl baś·śā·ḏeh wə·’ā·ḇî·ḵā ’îš mil·ḥā·māh wə·lō yā·lîn ’eṯ- hā·‘ām
verses.literal: He continued You know your father and his men . . . They are mighty men and as fierce . . . . . . as a wild bear robbed of her cubs Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops
verses.literalPt: Prosseguiu Husai: Tu sabes que teu pai e os homens que estão com ele são valentes e que estão com o espírito amargurado como a ursa no campo roubada dos seus cachorros. Teu pai é homem de guerra e não passará a noite com o povo.

verses.original: הִנֵּ֨ה עַתָּ֤ה הֽוּא־ נֶחְבָּא֙ בְּאַחַ֣ת הַפְּחָתִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקוֹמֹ֑ת וְהָיָ֗ה כִּנְפֹ֤ל בָּהֶם֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה וְשָׁמַ֤ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֙עַ֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הָֽיְתָה֙ מַגֵּפָ֔ה בָּעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃
verses.transliteration: hin·nêh ‘at·tāh hū- neḥ·bā bə·’a·ḥaṯ hap·pə·ḥā·ṯîm ’ōw bə·’a·ḥaḏ ham·mə·qō·w·mōṯ wə·hā·yāh kin·p̄ōl bā·hem bat·tə·ḥil·lāh wə·šā·ma‘ haš·šō·mê·a‘ wə·’ā·mar hā·yə·ṯāh mag·gê·p̄āh bā·‘ām ’ă·šer ’a·ḥă·rê ’aḇ·šā·lōm
verses.literal: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location If some of your troops fall first whoever hears of it . . . will say There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom
verses.literalPt: Eis que, agora, está ele escondido em alguma caverna ou em qualquer outro lugar; e, ao caírem alguns do povo no primeiro ataque, quem isso ouvir dirá: Há matança entre o povo que segue a Absalão.

verses.original: וְה֣וּא גַם־ בֶּן־ חַ֗יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִבּ֛וֹ כְּלֵ֥ב הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הִמֵּ֣ס יִמָּ֑ס כִּֽי־ יֹדֵ֤עַ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּי־ גִבּ֣וֹר אָבִ֔יךָ וּבְנֵי־ חַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hū ḡam- ben- ḥa·yil ’ă·šer lib·bōw kə·lêḇ hā·’ar·yêh him·mês yim·mās kî- yō·ḏê·a‘ kāl- yiś·rā·’êl kî- ḡib·bō·wr ’ā·ḇî·ḵā ū·ḇə·nê- ḥa·yil ’ă·šer ’it·tōw
verses.literal: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart . . . of a lion will melt with fear . . . because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him
verses.literalPt: Até o valente, cujo coração é como o dum leão, sem dúvida se derreterá. Porque todo o Israel sabe que teu pai é um herói e tem bravos consigo.

verses.original: כִּ֣י יָעַ֗צְתִּי הֵ֠אָסֹף יֵאָסֵ֨ף עָלֶ֤יךָ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וּפָנֶ֥יךָ הֹלְכִ֖ים בַּקְרָֽב׃
verses.transliteration: kî yā·‘aṣ·tî hê·’ā·sōp̄ yê·’ā·sêp̄ ‘ā·le·ḵā ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl mid·dān wə·‘aḏ- bə·’êr še·ḇa‘ ka·ḥō·wl ’ă·šer- ‘al- hay·yām lā·rōḇ ū·p̄ā·ne·ḵā hō·lə·ḵîm baq·rāḇ
verses.literal: Instead I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba a multitude like the sand on the seashore be gathered . . . to you and that you yourself lead them into battle
verses.literalPt: O meu conselho, porém, é que se ajunte a ti, sem demora, todo o Israel, desde Dã até Berseba, em multidão como a areia do mar; e que tu vás em pessoa no meio deles.

verses.original: וּבָ֣אנוּ אֵלָ֗יו בְּאַחַת הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְנַ֣חְנוּ עָלָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִפֹּ֥ל הַטַּ֖ל עַל־ הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ נ֥וֹתַר בּ֛וֹ וּבְכָל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ גַּם־ אֶחָֽד׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇā·nū ’ê·lāw bə·ʾa·ḥaṯ ham·mə·qō·w·mōṯ ’ă·šer nim·ṣā šām wə·naḥ·nū ‘ā·lāw ka·’ă·šer yip·pōl haṭ·ṭal ‘al- hā·’ă·ḏā·māh wə·lō- nō·w·ṯar bōw ū·ḇə·ḵāl hā·’ă·nā·šîm ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw gam- ’e·ḥāḏ
verses.literal: Then we will attack David wherever we find him . . . and we will descend on him like dew on the ground And of all the men with him not even one will remain
verses.literalPt: Assim, daremos sobre ele em qualquer lugar em que for achado e desceremos sobre ele como costuma cair o orvalho sobre a terra; não será deixado nem sequer um só homem dos que estão com ele.

verses.original: וְאִם־ אֶל־ עִיר֙ יֵֽאָסֵ֔ף וְהִשִּׂ֧יאוּ כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַהִ֖יא חֲבָלִ֑ים וְסָחַ֤בְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־ הַנַּ֔חַל עַ֛ד אֲשֶֽׁר־ לֹא־ נִמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם גַּם־ צְרֽוֹר׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·’im- ’el- ‘îr yê·’ā·sêp̄ wə·hiś·śî·’ū ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl ’el- hā·‘îr ha·hî ḥă·ḇā·lîm wə·sā·ḥaḇ·nū ’ō·ṯōw ‘aḏ- han·na·ḥal ‘aḏ ’ă·šer- lō- nim·ṣā šām gam- ṣə·rō·wr
verses.literal: If he retreats to a city all Israel will bring ropes to that city and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found there
verses.literalPt: Porém, se ele se retirar para alguma cidade, todo o Israel trará cordas àquela cidade, e arrastá-la-emos para o ribeiro, até que não se ache ali nem uma só pedrinha.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל טוֹבָ֗ה עֲצַת֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י מֵעֲצַ֖ת אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל וַיהוָ֣ה צִוָּ֗ה לְהָפֵ֞ר אֶת־ עֲצַ֤ת אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה לְבַעֲב֗וּר הָבִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶת־ הָרָעָֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm wə·ḵāl ’îš yiś·rā·’êl ṭō·w·ḇāh ‘ă·ṣaṯ ḥū·šay hā·’ar·kî mê·‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el Yah·weh ṣiw·wāh lə·hā·p̄êr ’eṯ- ‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el haṭ·ṭō·w·ḇāh lə·ḇa·‘ă·ḇūr hā·ḇî Yah·weh ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’eṯ- hā·rā·‘āh
verses.literal: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring . . . disaster on Absalom
verses.literalPt: Disse Absalão e todos os homens de Israel: O conselho de Husai, arquita, é melhor do que o de Aitofel. Pois Jeová ordenara que fosse dissipado o bom conselho de Aitofel, para trazer o mal sobre Absalão.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אֶל־ צָד֤וֹק וְאֶל־ אֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כָּזֹ֣את וְכָזֹ֗את יָעַ֤ץ אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָזֹ֥את וְכָזֹ֖את יָעַ֥צְתִּי אָֽנִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥū·šay ’el- ṣā·ḏō·wq wə·’el- ’eḇ·yā·ṯār hak·kō·hă·nîm kā·zōṯ wə·ḵā·zōṯ yā·‘aṣ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lōm wə·’êṯ ziq·nê yiś·rā·’êl wə·ḵā·zōṯ wə·ḵā·zōṯ yā·‘aṣ·tî ’ā·nî
verses.literal: So Hushai . . . told Zadok . . . and Abiathar the priests This is what . . . Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel and this is what . . . I have advised
verses.literalPt: Disse Husai ao sacerdote Zadoque e Abiatar: Assim e assim aconselhou Aitofel a Absalão e os anciãos de Israel; porém eu aconselhei assim e assim.

verses.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה שִׁלְח֣וּ מְהֵרָה֩ וְהַגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר אַל־ תָּ֤לֶן הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְגַ֖ם עָב֣וֹר תַּעֲב֑וֹר פֶּ֚ן יְבֻלַּ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·‘at·tāh šil·ḥū mə·hê·rāh wə·hag·gî·ḏū lə·ḏā·wiḏ lê·mōr ’al- tā·len hal·lay·lāh bə·‘ar·ḇō·wṯ ham·miḏ·bār wə·ḡam ‘ā·ḇō·wr ta·‘ă·ḇō·wr pen yə·ḇul·la‘ lam·me·leḵ ū·lə·ḵāl- hā·‘ām ’ă·šer ’it·tōw
verses.literal: Now send quickly and tell David . . . Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness but be sure to cross over . . . Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up
verses.literalPt: Agora, enviai depressa a avisar a Davi, dizendo: Não fiques esta noite nos vaus do deserto, mas, sem demora, atravessa para a outra banda; não suceda que seja engolido o rei e todo o povo que com ele está.

verses.original: וִיהוֹנָתָ֨ן וַאֲחִימַ֜עַץ עֹמְדִ֣ים בְּעֵין־ רֹגֵ֗ל וְהָלְכָ֤ה הַשִּׁפְחָה֙ וְהִגִּ֣ידָה לָהֶ֔ם וְהֵם֙ יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְהִגִּ֖ידוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֛וּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת לָב֥וֹא הָעִֽירָה׃
verses.transliteration: wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān wa·’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ ‘ō·mə·ḏîm bə·‘ên- rō·ḡêl wə·hā·lə·ḵāh haš·šip̄·ḥāh wə·hig·gî·ḏāh lā·hem wə·hêm yê·lə·ḵū wə·hig·gî·ḏū lam·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ kî lō yū·ḵə·lū lə·hê·rā·’ō·wṯ lā·ḇō·w hā·‘î·rāh
verses.literal: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them They in turn would go and inform King David for they dared not be seen entering the city
verses.literalPt: Ora, Jônatas e Aimaás estavam junto a En-Rogel; uma criada ia avisar-lhes, pois não podiam ser vistos entrar na cidade; eles partiram a dizer ao rei Davi.

verses.original: וַיַּ֤רְא אֹתָם֙ נַ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ שְׁנֵיהֶ֨ם מְהֵרָ֜ה וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ׀ אֶל־ בֵּֽית־ אִ֣ישׁ בְּבַחוּרִ֗ים וְל֥וֹ בְאֵ֛ר בַּחֲצֵר֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥רְדוּ שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar ’ō·ṯām na·‘ar way·yag·gêḏ lə·’aḇ·šā·lōm way·yê·lə·ḵū šə·nê·hem mə·hê·rāh way·yā·ḇō·’ū ’el- bêṯ- ’îš bə·ḇa·ḥū·rîm wə·lōw ḇə·’êr ba·ḥă·ṣê·rōw way·yê·rə·ḏū šām
verses.literal: But a young man did see them and told Absalom So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim He had a well in his courtyard and they climbed down into it
verses.literalPt: Viu-os, porém, um rapaz e avisou a Absalão. Mas ambos partiram às pressas e entraram em casa dum homem de Baurim, que tinha um poço no pátio de sua casa, ao qual desceram.

verses.original: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אֶת־ הַמָּסָךְ֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַתִּשְׁטַ֥ח עָלָ֖יו הָֽרִפ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע דָּבָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tiq·qaḥ hā·’iš·šāh wat·tip̄·rōś ’eṯ- ham·mā·sāḵ ‘al- pə·nê hab·bə·’êr wat·tiš·ṭaḥ ‘ā·lāw hā·ri·p̄ō·wṯ wə·lō nō·w·ḏa‘ dā·ḇār
verses.literal: Then the man’s wife took a covering spread it over the mouth of the well and scattered grain over it so nobody would know a thing
verses.literalPt: A mulher, tomando a tampa, estendeu-a sobre a boca do poço, espalhou frutas sobre ela; e nada se soube.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַבְדֵי֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶֽל־ הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבַּ֗יְתָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֗ה אֲחִימַ֙עַץ֙ וִיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה עָבְר֖וּ מִיכַ֣ל הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֔אוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō·’ū ‘aḇ·ḏê ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- hā·’iš·šāh hab·bay·ṯāh way·yō·mə·rū ’ay·yêh ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān wat·tō·mer lā·hem hā·’iš·šāh ‘ā·ḇə·rū mî·ḵal ham·mā·yim way·ḇaq·šū wə·lō mā·ṣā·’ū way·yā·šu·ḇū yə·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house they asked Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan They have crossed over the brook . . . she replied The men searched but did not find them so they returned to Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Chegando os servos de Absalão à casa da mulher, perguntaram: Onde estão Aimaás e Jônatas? Respondeu-lhes a mulher: Já passaram o ribeiro. Tendo-os procurado, sem os acharem, voltaram para Jerusalém.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ אַחֲרֵ֣י לֶכְתָּ֗ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ מֵֽהַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד ק֣וּמוּ וְעִבְר֤וּ מְהֵרָה֙ אֶת־ הַמַּ֔יִם כִּי־ כָ֛כָה יָעַ֥ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ’a·ḥă·rê leḵ·tām way·ya·‘ă·lū mê·hab·bə·’êr way·yê·lə·ḵū way·yag·gi·ḏū lam·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ way·yō·mə·rū ’el- dā·wiḏ qū·mū wə·‘iḇ·rū mə·hê·rāh ’eṯ- ham·ma·yim kî- ḵā·ḵāh yā·‘aṣ ‘ă·lê·ḵem ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el
verses.literal: After the men had gone Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David saying - Get up and cross over the river at once for Ahithophel has given this advice against you
verses.literalPt: Logo que se retiraram, saíram Aimaás e Jônatas do poço, e foram avisar o rei Davi, e disseram-lhe: Levantai-vos e passai depressa as águas, porque assim e assim aconselhou Aitofel contra vós.

verses.original: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן עַד־ א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר עַד־ אַחַד֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ עָבַ֖ר אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·qām dā·wiḏ wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ’ă·šer ’it·tōw way·ya·‘aḇ·rū ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên ‘aḏ- ’ō·wr hab·bō·qer ‘aḏ- ’a·ḥaḏ lō ne‘·dār ’ă·šer lō- ‘ā·ḇar ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên
verses.literal: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan By daybreak . . . . . . there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan
verses.literalPt: Então, se levantou Davi e todo o povo que estava com ele, e passaram o Jordão; antes de raiar o dia, não lhes faltava nem sequer um que não tivesse passado o Jordão.

verses.original: וַאֲחִיתֹ֣פֶל רָאָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נֶעֶשְׂתָה֮ עֲצָתוֹ֒ וַיַּחֲבֹ֣שׁ אֶֽת־ הַחֲמ֗וֹר וַיָּ֜קָם וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶל־ עִיר֔וֹ וַיְצַ֥ו אֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקֶ֥בֶר אָבִֽיו׃ס
verses.transliteration: wa·’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el rā·’āh kî lō ne·‘eś·ṯāh ‘ă·ṣā·ṯōw way·ya·ḥă·ḇōš ’eṯ- ha·ḥă·mō·wr way·yā·qām way·yê·leḵ ’el- bê·ṯōw ’el- ‘î·rōw way·ṣaw ’el- bê·ṯōw way·yê·ḥā·naq way·yā·māṯ way·yiq·qā·ḇêr bə·qe·ḇer ’ā·ḇîw
verses.literal: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed he saddled his donkey and set out . . . for his house in his hometown He put his affairs . . . in order and hanged himself So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb
verses.literalPt: Vendo Aitofel que não se havia seguido o seu conselho, albardou o seu jumento, e levantou-se, e foi para casa, para a sua cidade; tendo posto em ordem a sua casa, enforcou-se, morreu e foi enterrado na sepultura de seu pai.

verses.original: וְדָוִ֖ד בָּ֣א מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֗ם עָבַר֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן ה֕וּא וְכָל־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḏā·wiḏ bā ma·ḥă·nā·yə·māh wə·’aḇ·šā·lōm ‘ā·ḇar ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên hū wə·ḵāl ’îš yiś·rā·’êl ‘im·mōw
verses.literal: Then David went to Mahanaim and Absalom crossed the Jordan . . . with all the men of Israel
verses.literalPt: Davi chegou a Maanaim. Absalão, tendo passado o Jordão com todos os homens de Israel,

verses.original: וְאֶת־ עֲמָשָׂ֗א שָׂ֧ם אַבְשָׁלֹ֛ם תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָ֖ב עַל־ הַצָּבָ֑א וַעֲמָשָׂ֣א בֶן־ אִ֗ישׁ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יִתְרָ֣א הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־ בָּא֙ אֶל־ אֲבִיגַ֣ל בַּת־ נָחָ֔שׁ אֲח֥וֹת צְרוּיָ֖ה אֵ֥ם יוֹאָֽב׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’eṯ- ‘ă·mā·śā śām ’aḇ·šā·lōm ta·ḥaṯ yō·w·’āḇ ‘al- haṣ·ṣā·ḇā wa·‘ă·mā·śā ḇen- ’îš ū·šə·mōw yiṯ·rā hay·yiś·rə·’ê·lî ’ă·šer- bā ’el- ’ă·ḇî·ḡal baṯ- nā·ḥāš ’ă·ḥō·wṯ ṣə·rū·yāh ’êm yō·w·’āḇ
verses.literal: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Ishmaelite who had married . . . Abigail the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab
verses.literalPt: deu o mando do exército a Amasa em lugar de Joabe. Ora, Amasa era filho dum homem que se chamava Itra, israelita, que entrou a Abigail, filha de Naás, irmã de Zeruia, mãe de Joabe.

verses.original: וַיִּ֤חַן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם אֶ֖רֶץ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yi·ḥan yiś·rā·’êl wə·’aḇ·šā·lōm ’e·reṣ hag·gil·‘āḏ
verses.literal: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead
verses.literalPt: Israel e Absalão acamparam-se na terra de Gileade.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֕י כְּב֥וֹא דָוִ֖ד מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְשֹׁבִ֨י בֶן־ נָחָ֜שׁ מֵרַבַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ עַמּ֗וֹן וּמָכִ֤יר בֶּן־ עַמִּיאֵל֙ מִלֹּ֣א דְבָ֔ר וּבַרְזִלַּ֥י הַגִּלְעָדִ֖י מֵרֹגְלִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kə·ḇō·w ḏā·wiḏ ma·ḥă·nā·yə·māh wə·šō·ḇî ḇen- nā·ḥāš mê·rab·baṯ bə·nê- ‘am·mō·wn ū·mā·ḵîr ben- ‘am·mî·’êl mil·lō ḏə·ḇār ū·ḇar·zil·lay hag·gil·‘ā·ḏî mê·rō·ḡə·lîm
verses.literal: When David came to Mahanaim he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites . . . Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
verses.literalPt: Tendo Davi chegado a Maanaim, Sobi, filho de Naás, de Rabá que pertencia aos filhos de Amom, e Maquir, filho de Amiel, de Lo-Debar, e Barzilai, gileadita de Rogelim,

verses.original: מִשְׁכָּ֤ב וְסַפּוֹת֙ וּכְלִ֣י יוֹצֵ֔ר וְחִטִּ֥ים וּשְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְקֶ֣מַח וְקָלִ֑י וּפ֥וֹל וַעֲדָשִׁ֖ים וְקָלִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: miš·kāḇ wə·sap·pō·wṯ ū·ḵə·lî yō·w·ṣêr wə·ḥiṭ·ṭîm ū·śə·‘ō·rîm wə·qe·maḥ wə·qā·lî ū·p̄ō·wl wa·‘ă·ḏā·šîm wə·qā·lî
verses.literal: They brought beds basins and earthen vessels as well as wheat barley flour roasted grain beans lentils . . .
verses.literalPt: tomaram camas, bacias e louça de barro; trigo, cevada, farinha, grão torrado, favas e lentilhas também torradas;

verses.original: וּדְבַ֣שׁ וְחֶמְאָ֗ה וְצֹאן֙ וּשְׁפ֣וֹת בָּקָ֔ר הִגִּ֧ישׁוּ לְדָוִ֛ד וְלָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ הָעָ֗ם רָעֵ֛ב וְעָיֵ֥ף וְצָמֵ֖א בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḏə·ḇaš wə·ḥem·’āh wə·ṣōn ū·šə·p̄ō·wṯ bā·qār hig·gî·šū lə·ḏā·wiḏ wə·lā·‘ām ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw le·’ĕ·ḵō·wl kî ’ā·mə·rū hā·‘ām rā·‘êḇ wə·‘ā·yêp̄ wə·ṣā·mê bam·miḏ·bār
verses.literal: honey curds sheep and cheese from the herd . . . for David and his people - to eat For they said The people have become hungry exhausted and thirsty in the wilderness
verses.literalPt: e mel, coalhada, ovelhas e queijos de vacas, os quais trouxeram a Davi e ao povo que estava com ele, para que comessem. Porque disseram: O povo está faminto, cansado e sedento, no deserto.
